title: @talex-touch/tuffex ships CommonJS dist/lib inside a "type":"module" package; require() fails
summary: tuffex declares "type":"module" but its `main` and its `require` export condition both point at dist/lib/*.js, which the gulp build emits in CommonJS syntax. Node parses those .js files as ESM because of the package type, so every CJS consumer of the published package explodes on load.
evidence: packages/tuffex/package.json:17 "type": "module", :18 "main": "dist/lib/index.js", :25 "require": "./dist/lib/index.js"  —  packages/tuffex/dist/lib/index.js:1 `'use strict';` :3 `Object.defineProperties(exports, { __esModule: { value: true }, ... });` :5 `const components = require('./components.js');`
failure_scenario: Reproduced on Node 24.18.0: importing packages/tuffex/dist/lib/index.js throws `exports is not defined in ES module scope. This file is being treated as an ES module because it has a '.js' file extension and '.../packages/tuffex/package.json' contains "type": "module". To treat it as a CommonJS script, rename it to use the '.cjs' file extension.` Any external consumer doing require('@talex-touch/tuffex') or bundling with the `require` condition (Jest, webpack CJS output, Electron main without ESM) fails at load. tuffex is published to npm (v0.3.9, MIT, files:[dist]).
recommendation: Emit dist/lib as .cjs (or add a dist/lib/package.json with {"type":"commonjs"}) and point the `require` condition at it.

title: Published @talex-touch/utils has main:"index.ts"; Node 24 cannot load it
summary: @talex-touch/utils is a public npm package (private:false, v1.0.50) whose entry point is a raw TypeScript file using ESM `export *` with extensionless directory specifiers. Node 24 strips the types, treats the file as ESM, and then cannot resolve the directory re-exports.
evidence: packages/utils/package.json:18 "main": "index.ts", :19 "module": "./index.ts", :4 "private": false  —  packages/utils/index.ts:2 `export * from './account'` (extensionless directory specifier, no `exports` map and no `types` field in package.json)
failure_scenario: Reproduced on Node 24.18.0: `require('@talex-touch/utils')` throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT: Directory import '.../packages/utils/account' is not supported resolving ES modules imported from .../packages/utils/index.ts`. Any external plugin developer consuming the published package from plain Node, or from any bundler that does not alias TS sources, cannot import it at all — only the in-repo electron-vite/Vite aliases make it work.
recommendation: Publish a built dist (ESM+CJS+.d.ts) with an `exports` map, or at minimum add explicit file extensions and an `exports` field.

title: touch-image installs unplugin-export-plugin 0.2.13 from npm, not the workspace 1.2.16
summary: touch-image declares a semver range instead of `workspace:*`, and the range excludes the workspace version, so pnpm installs the pre-1.0 registry copy alongside the local one.
evidence: plugins/touch-image/package.json:48 `"@talex-touch/unplugin-export-plugin": "^0.2.13",` while packages/unplugin-export-plugin/package.json:4 is `"version": "1.2.16"`. pnpm-lock.yaml:1189 records `specifier: ^0.2.13 / version: 0.2.13` and pnpm-lock.yaml:5409 `'@talex-touch/unplugin-export-plugin@0.2.13': resolution: {integrity: sha512-Jh8jwvkcreTrKhua2xbqfWE+...}` — a registry tarball, not a workspace link.
failure_scenario: Building plugins/touch-image runs the 0.2.13 plugin, which predates every API change made in 1.x (the sibling plugin touch-translation uses `workspace:^`). Fixes and manifest-schema changes landed in the workspace package silently do not apply to touch-image, and the two plugins emit packages built by different, incompatible builders.
recommendation: Change to `"@talex-touch/unplugin-export-plugin": "workspace:^"` to match plugins/touch-translation.

title: Catalog pins @langchain/langgraph ^0.2.74 while every consumer hard-codes ^0.4.9
summary: The shared catalog entry for langgraph is two breaking minors behind what the code actually installs, and no package references it via `catalog:`, so the catalog is stale documentation that will silently downgrade anything that starts using it.
evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml:41 `'@langchain/langgraph': ^0.2.74` — but apps/core-app/package.json:99, apps/nexus/package.json:48 and packages/tuff-intelligence/package.json:56 all declare `"@langchain/langgraph": "^0.4.9"` literally. A repo-wide grep for `"@langchain/langgraph": "catalog:"` returns 0 hits.
failure_scenario: The moment any package switches to `catalog:` (the stated convention for shared deps) pnpm installs 0.2.74. LangGraph is pre-1.0, so 0.2 → 0.4 crosses two breaking-change boundaries: the 0.4 graph/state APIs used in packages/tuff-intelligence do not exist in 0.2.74 and the build fails to typecheck.
recommendation: Update the catalog entry to ^0.4.9 and switch the three consumers to `catalog:`.

title: Catalog pins @langchain/openai ^0.3.17 while every consumer hard-codes ^0.4.9
summary: Same drift as langgraph: the catalog entry is a breaking minor behind the version actually installed, and nothing references it via `catalog:`.
evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml:42 `'@langchain/openai': ^0.3.17` versus apps/core-app/package.json:100 `"@langchain/openai": "^0.4.9"` and apps/nexus/package.json:49 `"@langchain/openai": "^0.4.9"`. Grep for `"@langchain/openai": "catalog:"` returns 0 hits.
failure_scenario: Adopting `catalog:` for @langchain/openai downgrades to 0.3.17, whose peer range and ChatOpenAI option shape differ from 0.4.x; the AI provider wiring in apps/core-app/src/main/modules/ai stops typechecking against @langchain/core 0.3.80.
recommendation: Bump the catalog entry to ^0.4.9 (or delete the entry if the catalog is not intended to cover it).

title: Catalog pins next-auth ~4.21.1 while apps/nexus installs ~4.24.14
summary: Two contradictory next-auth pins exist in pnpm-workspace.yaml (the main catalog and a generated conflicts_ catalog), neither is referenced by any package, and the real consumer hard-codes a third literal range.
evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml:54 `next-auth: ~4.21.1`, pnpm-workspace.yaml:102-103 `conflicts_next-auth_t4_24_14: next-auth: ~4.24.14`, apps/nexus/package.json:88 `"next-auth": "~4.24.14"`. package.json:208 then widens the peer check with `"next-auth": "~4.21.1 || ~4.24.14"`. Grep for `"next-auth": "catalog:` returns 0 hits.
failure_scenario: The catalog claims 4.21.x is the supported version while the app runs 4.24.x. @sidebase/nuxt-auth 0.9.4 peers on next-auth 4.21.x; the allowedVersions escape hatch silences the mismatch instead of resolving it, so a genuine 4.21-vs-4.24 API break in the auth handler (apps/nexus/nuxt.config.ts:48 reaches into next-auth/core/index.js directly) surfaces only at runtime.
recommendation: Delete the conflicts_ catalog, set the single catalog entry to ~4.24.14, and have apps/nexus use `catalog:`.

title: nodemailer: catalog says ^9.0.3, peer rule allows only ^6||^7, and it is not installed at all
summary: Three sources disagree about nodemailer and none of them match reality: the catalog pins ^9.0.3, the peerDependencyRules allow ^6.6.5||^7.0.0 (which ^9.0.3 does not satisfy), and the package is absent from the lockfile.
evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml:55 `nodemailer: ^9.0.3`; package.json:207 `"nodemailer": "^6.6.5 || ^7.0.0"` under pnpm.peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions; pnpm-lock.yaml:1541 and :10546 record the peer requirement `nodemailer: ^7` / `^7.0.7` from @auth/core and next-auth, but `grep -n '^  nodemailer@' pnpm-lock.yaml` returns no snapshot — nothing is installed (auto-install-peers=false, .npmrc:2).
failure_scenario: Any code path in apps/nexus that reaches the @auth/core or next-auth Email provider throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at runtime because nodemailer was never installed. If someone fixes that by adopting `catalog:`, they get ^9.0.3, which is outside the ^7 peer range the providers declare and outside the allowedVersions override, so the peer warning returns.
recommendation: Decide whether the email provider is used: either add nodemailer ^7 as a real dependency of apps/nexus and align both entries, or delete the catalog entry and the allowedVersions rule.

title: Three incompatible majors of marked installed simultaneously (12.0.2, 16.4.2, 17.0.6)
summary: tuffex pins marked ^12 while @talex-touch/utils and the root toolchain pin ^17, and a third copy at 16.4.2 is pulled transitively. The core-app renderer bundles both tuffex and utils, so two markdown engines with different renderer/extension APIs ship in one bundle.
evidence: packages/tuffex/package.json:84 `"marked": "^12.0.2",` vs packages/utils/package.json:64 `"marked": "^17.0.6",` and package.json:? root devDependency `"marked": "17.0.6"`. pnpm-lock.yaml:10111/10116/10121 record `marked@12.0.2`, `marked@16.4.2`, `marked@17.0.6` as three distinct snapshots.
failure_scenario: marked 13 removed the sync/async `parse` overloads and 14-16 reworked the tokenizer/renderer extension signatures. tuffex's TxStreamMarkdown renderer extensions are written against v12 and would break if hoisting ever resolves it to 17; conversely utils' markdown helpers cannot run on 12. Both are bundled into the same Electron renderer output, duplicating ~50KB and producing inconsistent rendering between tuffex and utils code paths.
recommendation: Align tuffex to marked ^17 (or move marked to a catalog entry so one version is enforced).

title: compressing pinned to incompatible majors: ^1.10.5 in tuff-cli/tuff-cli-core vs ^2.1.1 in core-app
summary: The plugin builder CLI and the app that consumes its output use different majors of the archive library, and both are installed.
evidence: packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:37 `"compressing": "^1.10.5",` and packages/tuff-cli/package.json:35 `"compressing": "^1.10.5",` versus apps/core-app/package.json:112 `"compressing": "^2.1.1",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:7272/7276 record both `compressing@1.10.5` and `compressing@2.1.1`.
failure_scenario: compressing 2.x dropped Node <18 support and changed the stream/promise API surface; the plugin `.touch-plugin` archives are written by tuff-cli on v1 and unpacked by core-app on v2. Any format or option divergence between the two majors (e.g. zip entry mode handling) shows up only when a plugin built by the CLI is installed into the app.
recommendation: Bump tuff-cli and tuff-cli-core to compressing ^2.1.1 so writer and reader share one implementation.

title: tuff-cli-core declares @types/node ^18.19.130 under a Node >=24.15 workspace
summary: The package declares Node 18 typings but a global pnpm override silently swaps in 24.13.2, so it typechecks green in-repo against APIs its own manifest says are unavailable.
evidence: packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:48 `"@types/node": "^18.19.130",` while package.json:134 forces `"@types/node": "24.13.2"` in pnpm.overrides and package.json:10 declares `"engines": {"node": ">=24.15.0"}`. The package's own engines field (packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:21) says `">=24.0.0"`.
failure_scenario: Inside the workspace the override hides the mismatch. Building this package outside the monorepo (or after the override is removed) installs @types/node 18, and any Node 20+/22+ API used in src — e.g. `node:fs/promises` additions, `structuredClone`, glob options — fails to typecheck with 'Property does not exist'. The declared range also misrepresents the package's real runtime requirement to anyone reading the manifest.
recommendation: Set @types/node to ^24.13.2 to match engines and the override.

title: unplugin-export-plugin (published v1.2.16) declares @types/node ^18.19.130 under a Node 24 workspace
summary: A publicly published build plugin pins Node 18 typings while the workspace override forces 24.13.2, so its declared type baseline is never actually exercised.
evidence: packages/unplugin-export-plugin/package.json:78 `"@types/node": "^18.19.130",` with package.json:4 `"version": "1.2.16"` and publishConfig-less public publish via :64 `"release": "bumpp && npm publish --access public"`. Root package.json:134 overrides `"@types/node": "24.13.2"`.
failure_scenario: Contributors building this package standalone (the documented `pnpm unplugin:build`) outside the workspace get @types/node 18 and lose typings for anything added in Node 20-24; conversely code written against the overridden 24.x typings compiles in-repo but its declared devDependency claims Node 18 compatibility that was never verified.
recommendation: Align @types/node with the workspace override (^24.13.2) or drop the pin and rely on the catalog.

title: tuffex declares @types/node ^22.20.0, a third distinct Node typings baseline in the monorepo
summary: The monorepo carries three declared @types/node baselines (18, 22, 24) that are all silently collapsed to 24.13.2 by a root override, so none of the declarations is meaningful.
evidence: packages/tuffex/package.json:94 `"@types/node": "^22.20.0",` vs packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:48 `"^18.19.130"` vs plugins/touch-translation/package.json:28 `"^24.13.2"`, all overridden by package.json:134 `"@types/node": "24.13.2"`.
failure_scenario: tuffex's tsconfig.json:17 sets `"types": ["vite/client", "node"]`, so its vue-tsc run resolves whatever @types/node the override supplies (24.x) rather than the declared 22.x. Removing the override — or building tuffex standalone for the npm publish workflow — changes the ambient Node typings under the components and can surface new errors that CI never saw.
recommendation: Standardise every package on ^24.13.2 (ideally via a `catalog:` entry) so the override becomes redundant.

title: core-app renderer imports 6 undeclared runtime packages (pinia, vue-i18n, @vueuse/core, gsap)
summary: The shipped Electron renderer imports six third-party packages that appear nowhere in apps/core-app's dependencies/devDependencies. They resolve only because .npmrc sets shamefully-hoist=true and other workspace packages happen to pull them in.
evidence: None of `pinia`, `vue-i18n`, `@vueuse/core`, `gsap`, `@floating-ui/vue`, `path-browserify` appear in apps/core-app/package.json (grep count 0 each). Import sites: apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/main.ts:10 `import { createPinia } from 'pinia'`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/composables/usePermissionStartup.ts:10 `import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n'`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/App.vue:3 `import { until } from '@vueuse/core'`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/components/tuff/TuffGroupBlock.vue:3 `import gsap from 'gsap'`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/components/base/select/TSelect.vue:2 `import { computePosition } from '@floating-ui/vue'`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/views/box/tag/FileTag.vue:2 `import path from 'path-browserify'`.
failure_scenario: Turning off .npmrc:1 `shamefully-hoist=true` (pnpm default strict layout) makes `pnpm core:build` fail immediately with Vite 'Failed to resolve import "pinia" from src/renderer/src/main.ts'. Today all six resolve from the hoisted root tree (pinia@3.0.4, vue-i18n@11.4.0, @vueuse/core@14.3.0, gsap@3.15.0, @floating-ui/vue@1.1.11, path-browserify@1.0.1) — versions chosen by apps/nexus and packages/tuffex, not by core-app. vue-i18n in particular is present only as an optional peer of @intlify/unplugin-vue-i18n and @nuxtjs/i18n (a nexus devDependency), so the shipped Electron app's i18n runtime version is decided by the docs site.
recommendation: Add all six to apps/core-app dependencies with explicit ranges (pinia and @vueuse/core via `catalog:frontend`).

title: electron.vite.config.ts imports 7 build plugins that apps/core-app does not declare
summary: The core-app build config depends on Vite/UnoCSS/unplugin packages that are absent from its manifest; the build only works because of workspace-wide hoisting.
evidence: apps/core-app/electron.vite.config.ts:5-14 `import VueI18nPlugin from '@intlify/unplugin-vue-i18n/vite'`, `import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'`, `import vueJsx from '@vitejs/plugin-vue-jsx'`, `import type { Plugin } from 'vite'`, `import Unocss from 'unocss/vite'`, `import AutoImport from 'unplugin-auto-import/vite'`, `import Components from 'unplugin-vue-components/vite'`. grep for each of `@intlify/unplugin-vue-i18n`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue-jsx`, `unocss`, `unplugin-auto-import`, `unplugin-vue-components`, `vite` in apps/core-app/package.json returns 0.
failure_scenario: A clean install with pnpm's default (non-hoisted) node_modules, or a CI job that installs only the core-app filter (`pnpm -F @talex-touch/core-app install`), cannot load electron.vite.config.ts — `Cannot find package '@vitejs/plugin-vue'`. Vite 7 majors also arrive uncontrolled: the plugin versions come from whichever sibling package resolves them.
recommendation: Declare all seven in apps/core-app devDependencies, using `catalog:build` for vite/unocss.

title: core-app main process imports undeclared `plist` and `chalk`
summary: Two main-process runtime imports are not in apps/core-app's manifest. They currently survive packaging only because electron-vite's externalizeDepsPlugin externalizes declared dependencies only, so undeclared ones get inlined by accident.
evidence: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/box-tool/addon/files/services/file-provider-opener-service.ts:12 `import plist from 'plist'` and apps/core-app/src/main/utils/logger.ts:2 `import chalk from 'chalk'`. Neither `"plist"` nor `"chalk"` appears in apps/core-app/package.json (grep count 0). Note the manifest does declare a different package, `"simple-plist": "1.4.0"` (line 130).
failure_scenario: The behaviour is version-uncontrolled and fragile in both directions: today rollup inlines them (they are invisible to externalizeDepsPlugin at apps/core-app/electron.vite.config.ts:171), but the moment either is added to `dependencies` it becomes external and must exist in node_modules at runtime — and electron-builder.yml:159 sets `npmRebuild: false` with `files: node_modules/**` scoped to core-app, so a missing entry becomes a production MODULE_NOT_FOUND. A strict (non-hoisted) install breaks the build outright.
recommendation: Declare `plist` and `chalk` explicitly in apps/core-app dependencies.

title: .npmrc shamefully-hoist=true masks 18 undeclared dependencies in apps/core-app alone
summary: The workspace disables pnpm's strict node_modules isolation, which is the single reason 18 phantom dependencies resolves. It converts every missing manifest entry from an install-time error into a silent, version-uncontrolled binding.
evidence: .npmrc:1 `shamefully-hoist=true` combined with .npmrc:2 `auto-install-peers=false`. Scanning apps/core-app bare imports against its manifest yields 18 undeclared specifiers: 11 from src (pinia, vue-i18n, @vueuse/core, gsap, @floating-ui/vue, path-browserify, plist, chalk, electron, vitest, @vue/test-utils) and 7 from electron.vite.config.ts (@intlify/unplugin-vue-i18n, @vitejs/plugin-vue, @vitejs/plugin-vue-jsx, unocss, unplugin-auto-import, unplugin-vue-components, vite).
failure_scenario: Because hoisting is global, the resolved version of each phantom dependency is decided by whichever unrelated workspace package pulls it in. Bumping @talex-touch/tuffex's `gsap` or `@floating-ui/vue`, or apps/nexus's `pinia`, silently changes what the shipped Electron renderer bundles, with no entry in apps/core-app's lockfile importer to review. Removing the flag (or publishing any affected package) surfaces all 18 at once as unresolved-import build errors.
recommendation: Fix the phantom dependencies first, then drop shamefully-hoist (keep a narrow public-hoist-pattern for electron only, which .npmrc:3 already has).

title: safe-path.isAbsolutePath() throws TypeError in browser contexts: path-browserify win32 is null
summary: The shared path-safety helper falls back to path-browserify whenever `window` exists, then dereferences `path.win32`, which path-browserify sets to null.
evidence: packages/utils/common/utils/safe-path.ts:5-6 `if (hasWindow()) { return pathBrowserify }` and :34 `return path.isAbsolute(value) || path.win32.isAbsolute(value)`. Verified on the installed path-browserify@1.0.1: `require('path-browserify').win32` is `null`, and calling `.isAbsolute` on it throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'isAbsolute')`. `hasWindow()` is `typeof window !== 'undefined'` (packages/utils/env/index.ts:79-81), which is true in the renderer, in preload, and in every plugin Surface WebContents.
failure_scenario: In a window context, `isAbsolutePath()` and therefore `normalizeAbsolutePath()` crash for any input that is not POSIX-absolute — i.e. every Windows path ('C:\\Users\\me\\file.txt') and every relative path — because the `||` only short-circuits when path.isAbsolute() is true. @talex-touch/utils is published for third-party plugin authors whose Surface code runs in exactly that context.
recommendation: Guard the win32 branch (`path.win32?.isAbsolute?.(value) ?? false`) or use an explicit drive-letter regex instead of relying on path-browserify's win32 shim.

title: Three renderer components use path-browserify on absolute paths, producing wrong output on Windows
summary: CoreBox file chips and result subtitles call basename/dirname/extname from path-browserify, which only understands '/' separators. On Windows the main process supplies backslash paths, so the UI shows the entire path instead of a file name.
evidence: apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/views/box/tag/FileTag.vue:27 `return path.basename(firstPath || '')`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/views/box/tag/UnifiedFileTag.vue:86 `return path.basename(filePaths.value[0])` and :67 `return path.extname(value).replace(/^\./, '').toLowerCase()`; apps/core-app/src/renderer/src/components/render/ItemSubtitle.vue:121 `{{ path.dirname(fileInfo.path).split('/').pop() }}` — all importing `path from 'path-browserify'`.
failure_scenario: Verified against the installed path-browserify@1.0.1 (sep === '/'): `basename('C:\\Users\\me\\Documents\\report.txt')` returns the full unchanged string and `dirname(...)` returns '.'. On Windows, every CoreBox file result chip renders the complete absolute path instead of 'report.txt', and ItemSubtitle renders '.' as the containing folder. macOS/Linux are unaffected, which is why it has not been caught.
recommendation: Send a pre-computed display name from the main process (where node:path is available), or split on /[\\\\/]/ in the renderer.

title: @talex-touch/utils lists vue as both a dependency and a peerDependency, risking duplicate Vue copies
summary: The published utils package declares vue as a hard dependency (^3.5.39) while also declaring it as a peer (^3.5.27). Consumers therefore get a second Vue instance nested under node_modules/@talex-touch/utils.
evidence: packages/utils/package.json:59 `"vue": "^3.5.27"` under peerDependencies and :67 `"vue": "^3.5.39"` under dependencies, in a package with :4 `"private": false` and :3 `"version": "1.0.50"`.
failure_scenario: Under pnpm's isolated layout (or any consumer whose app Vue version differs), utils' composables in packages/utils/renderer run against their own Vue instance. Reactivity created inside utils is invisible to the host app, `inject()`/`provide()` across the boundary returns undefined, and Vue logs 'You are running multiple copies of Vue'. In this repo the symptom is currently hidden by .npmrc shamefully-hoist=true.
recommendation: Remove `vue` from dependencies and keep only the peerDependency (add it to devDependencies for local typechecking).

title: @talex-touch/tuff-intelligence lists zod as both an exact dependency and a peerDependency
summary: zod is pinned exactly (3.25.76) in dependencies and simultaneously declared as a peer (^3.25.32), so consumers can end up with two zod copies and cross-copy instanceof/schema checks fail.
evidence: packages/tuff-intelligence/package.json:58 `"zod": "3.25.76"` under dependencies and :61 `"zod": "^3.25.32"` under peerDependencies, in a package published with :71 `"publishConfig": {"access": "public"}`.
failure_scenario: zod schemas are identity-sensitive: a ZodType produced by one copy fails `instanceof` in another, and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (apps/core-app dependency, peer `zod: ^3.25 || ^4.0`) validates tool schemas by exactly that mechanism. A consumer on zod 3.26 gets the peer satisfied but still receives the nested exact 3.25.76 copy, so tool-schema validation silently rejects valid schemas.
recommendation: Keep zod only as a peerDependency (plus devDependency), or drop the peer and keep a caret range dependency — not both.

title: core-app depends on deprecated xterm@5.3.0 and xterm-addon-fit@0.8.0 (renamed to @xterm/*)
summary: The terminal UI uses the retired `xterm` package name, which upstream deprecated in favour of the @xterm scope; the old name receives no fixes.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:135 `"xterm": "^5.3.0",` :136 `"xterm-addon-fit": "^0.8.0"`. pnpm-lock.yaml:13819 `xterm@5.3.0: ... deprecated: This package is now deprecated. Move to @xterm/xterm instead.` and pnpm-lock.yaml:13813 `xterm-addon-fit@0.8.0: ... deprecated: This package is now deprecated. Move to @xterm/addon-fit instead.` No @xterm scope is installed anywhere in the workspace.
failure_scenario: xterm 5.3.0 is frozen at the 2023 release. The terminal module (apps/core-app/src/main/modules/terminal) is stuck without the @xterm/xterm 5.5+ fixes for Chromium canvas/WebGL renderer changes, and every install emits a deprecation warning. Any future Electron/Chromium change to canvas text metrics cannot be fixed by upgrading, only by migrating the package name.
recommendation: Migrate to @xterm/xterm and @xterm/addon-fit (import path and addon class names change).

title: plugins/touch-music also pins deprecated xterm@5.3.0 / xterm-addon-fit@0.8.0
summary: The music plugin carries the same retired xterm packages as core-app, and it does not appear to render a terminal at all.
evidence: plugins/touch-music/package.json:26 `"xterm": "^5.3.0",` :27 `"xterm-addon-fit": "^0.8.0"`, both flagged in pnpm-lock.yaml:13819/13813 as `deprecated: This package is now deprecated. Move to @xterm/xterm instead.`
failure_scenario: The plugin bundles a deprecated, unmaintained terminal emulator (~300KB) into its Surface build. Because the dependency is unused by the plugin's feature set, it is pure deprecated surface area that will keep failing dependency audits and blocks the @xterm migration from being completed repo-wide.
recommendation: Remove xterm/xterm-addon-fit from touch-music if unused, otherwise migrate with core-app.

title: tuff-cli and tuff-cli-core depend on deprecated glob@10.5.0 flagged for known vulnerabilities
summary: Both CLI packages declare glob ^10, which npm marks deprecated with an explicit security notice; glob 11 is the supported line.
evidence: packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:40 `"glob": "^10.5.0",` and packages/tuff-cli/package.json:39 `"glob": "^10.5.0",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:8931 `glob@10.5.0: ... deprecated: Old versions of glob are not supported, and contain widely publicized security vulnerabilities, which have been fixed in the current version. Please update.`
failure_scenario: @talex-touch/tuff-cli is published to npm (v0.0.7, publishConfig access public) and is the documented plugin build tool, so every plugin author installs the deprecated glob transitively. Installs emit the deprecation warning and the package cannot receive upstream fixes without a major bump.
recommendation: Move both packages to glob ^11 (the v10 to v11 API is compatible for the patterns used here) and drop the unused @types/glob ^8.1.0 pin.

title: touch-translation depends on deprecated unplugin-vue-router@0.16.2 (merged into vue-router v5)
summary: The translation plugin's route generation relies on a package upstream has retired by folding it into vue-router itself.
evidence: plugins/touch-translation/package.json:42 `"unplugin-vue-router": "^0.16.2",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:12990 `unplugin-vue-router@0.16.2: ... deprecated: 'Merged into vuejs/router. Migrate: https://router.vuejs.org/guide/migration/v4-to-v5.html'`. The plugin runs vue-router ^4.6.4 (plugins/touch-translation/package.json:23).
failure_scenario: The plugin's build is pinned to an abandoned route generator while the rest of the workspace stays on vue-router 4. When core-app moves to vue-router 5 (apps/core-app/package.json:133 also pins ^4.6.4), the deprecated plugin's generated route types diverge from the router's built-in typed routes and the plugin Surface fails to typecheck (`vue-tsc --noEmit`, plugins/touch-translation/package.json:12).
recommendation: Follow the upstream v4-to-v5 migration and drop unplugin-vue-router, or pin the plugin's build to the last compatible combination and document it.

title: touch-translation uses unplugin-vue-macros ^2.x whose @vue-macros core is deprecated
summary: The 2.x macro toolchain resolves to @vue-macros packages that upstream marks deprecated in favour of v3.
evidence: plugins/touch-translation/package.json:41 `"unplugin-vue-macros": "^2.14.5",`. pnpm-lock.yaml:6153-6155 `'@vue-macros/define-props@4.0.6': ... deprecated: Use v3` with `peerDependencies: '@vue-macros/reactivity-transform': ^1.1.6`.
failure_scenario: The macro transforms run inside the plugin's Vite 7 build against Vue 3.5. The deprecated 2.x line will not receive fixes for Vue 3.6+ compiler-sfc changes, so the plugin's Surface build breaks on the next Vue minor while every other workspace package (which uses no macros) keeps building.
recommendation: Upgrade to unplugin-vue-macros v3, or remove the macro plugin if the plugin does not actually use the macros.

title: @ungap/structured-clone@1.3.0 (deprecated, CWE-502) is installed but not pinned by overrides
summary: The root pnpm.overrides block pins ~70 transitive packages for exactly this class of problem, yet a transitive dependency carrying an explicit deprecation-with-CVE notice is not among them.
evidence: pnpm-lock.yaml:5785-5787 `'@ungap/structured-clone@1.3.0': resolution: ... deprecated: Potential CWE-502 - Update to 1.3.1 or higher`. The root override list (package.json:133-195) pins node-forge, form-data, cookie, tar, ws, qs, follow-redirects and many others, but contains no `@ungap/structured-clone` entry.
failure_scenario: @ungap/structured-clone is pulled in through the remark/rehype chain used by apps/nexus content rendering and the root markdown tooling. Its 1.3.0 deserialization path is the flagged CWE-502 vector, and because there is no override, every fresh install keeps resolving 1.3.0 rather than the fixed 1.3.1.
recommendation: Add `"@ungap/structured-clone": "1.3.1"` to pnpm.overrides alongside the existing transitive pins.

title: Three publicly published packages declare no engines field despite a Node >=24.15 workspace
summary: @talex-touch/utils, @talex-touch/tuffex and @talex-touch/unplugin-export-plugin are all published to npm without an engines field, so npm/pnpm cannot warn consumers who are on an unsupported Node.
evidence: packages/utils/package.json (v1.0.50, `"private": false`) has no `engines` key; packages/tuffex/package.json (v0.3.9) has no `engines` key; packages/unplugin-export-plugin/package.json (v1.2.16) has no `engines` key. The root manifest declares package.json:10 `"engines": {"node": ">=24.15.0"}`, and the sibling published packages tuff-cli/tuff-core/tuff-intelligence do declare `">=24.0.0"`.
failure_scenario: An external plugin author on Node 20 installs @talex-touch/utils with no warning, then hits the ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT/type-stripping failure at require time instead of a clear EBADENGINE message at install time. The same applies to unplugin-export-plugin, whose tsup build output targets modern Node.
recommendation: Add `"engines": {"node": ">=24.15.0"}` to all three published manifests (or the lowest version actually supported).

title: Four packages declare engines node >=24.0.0 while the workspace root requires >=24.15.0
summary: The published sub-packages advertise a Node floor 15 patch releases below what the repository itself mandates, so their declared support window is untested.
evidence: packages/tuff-cli/package.json:22 `"node": ">=24.0.0"`, packages/tuff-cli-core/package.json:21 `"node": ">=24.0.0"`, packages/tuff-core/package.json:19 `"node": ">=24.0.0"`, packages/tuff-intelligence/package.json:45 `"node": ">=24.0.0"` versus root package.json:10 `"node": ">=24.15.0"`, .node-version `24.18.0`, and mise.toml:2 `node = "24.18.0"`.
failure_scenario: CI never runs on 24.0-24.14 (all workflows use `node-version-file: .node-version` = 24.18.0), so the advertised range is unverified. A consumer on Node 24.0 installs @talex-touch/tuff-cli without an EBADENGINE warning and can hit any 24.x behaviour change the code implicitly relies on.
recommendation: Raise all four to `>=24.15.0` to match the root engines declaration.

title: drizzle-kit is not installed anywhere; the documented db:generate/db:migrate scripts fail
summary: Two npm scripts and the drizzle config file depend on drizzle-kit, but it is declared in no manifest and has no entry in the lockfile.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:31 `"db:generate": "drizzle-kit generate",` :32 `"db:migrate": "drizzle-kit migrate",` and apps/core-app/drizzle.config.ts:1 `import type { Config } from 'drizzle-kit'`. `grep -n drizzle apps/core-app/package.json` shows only those two scripts plus :115 `"drizzle-orm": "^0.45.2"` — no drizzle-kit dependency. `grep -c drizzle-kit pnpm-lock.yaml` returns 0.
failure_scenario: `pnpm -F @talex-touch/core-app run db:generate` exits with 'drizzle-kit: command not found'. CLAUDE.md documents both commands as the supported way to create and apply migrations, so schema changes in src/main/db/schema.ts cannot be turned into migrations without a manual global install. drizzle.config.ts also fails to resolve its type import if it is ever added to a tsconfig include list.
recommendation: Add `drizzle-kit` (matching the drizzle-orm 0.45.x line) to apps/core-app devDependencies.

title: pnpm overrides force @sentry/electron onto 10.65.0 despite its exact 10.62.0 pins
summary: @sentry/electron 7.15.0 declares its Sentry sub-packages with exact (non-range) versions, signalling a matched-set requirement. Three targeted overrides push them a minor forward, which is exactly the kind of conflict overrides are supposed to surface rather than bury.
evidence: package.json:131-133 `"@sentry/electron>@sentry/browser": "10.65.0", "@sentry/electron>@sentry/core": "10.65.0", "@sentry/electron>@sentry/node": "10.65.0"`. node_modules/@sentry/electron/package.json declares `dependencies: {"@sentry/browser":"10.62.0","@sentry/core":"10.62.0","@sentry/node":"10.62.0"}` (exact pins) and `peerDependencies: {"@sentry/node-native":"10.62.0"}`. Installed tree: @sentry/electron 7.15.0 with @sentry/node, @sentry/core and @sentry/browser all at 10.65.0; @sentry/node-native is NOT INSTALLED.
failure_scenario: Sentry ships its JS SDK packages as a version-locked set; @sentry/electron's Electron-specific integrations are compiled against @sentry/core 10.62.0 internals (client, scope and transport plumbing that change between minors without a semver-major). Running them against 10.65.0 can break event enrichment or crash-report attachment silently at runtime. It also creates an unsatisfiable state for the optional @sentry/node-native peer, which demands exactly 10.62.0 while the rest of the stack is forced to 10.65.0.
recommendation: Drop the three overrides and upgrade @sentry/electron to a release that already depends on 10.65.0, so the matched set stays intact.

title: electron-builder macOS target is `dir` on arm64 only — no installable artifact and no Intel build
summary: The mac target produces an unpacked directory for arm64 only, while a dmg config block and a GitHub publish provider are configured and the release workflow searches for .dmg/.zip artifacts.
evidence: apps/core-app/electron-builder.yml:120-122 `target:\n    - target: dir\n      arch: arm64` with :128 an empty `dmg:` block and :163-166 `publish: provider: github`. .github/workflows/build-and-release.yml:563 `DMG_COUNT=$(find apps/core-app/dist -name "*.dmg" -type f ...)` and :565 `ZIP_COUNT=$(find apps/core-app/dist -name "*.zip" ...)`. apps/core-app/scripts/build-target.js:501 `const defaultArch = normalizedTarget === 'mac' ? 'arm64' : 'x64'` — no target override is injected.
failure_scenario: `pnpm core:build:release:mac` (and the macOS release job) emit only `dist/mac-arm64/tuff.app`. DMG_COUNT and ZIP_COUNT are both 0, so the release publishes no macOS installer, and Intel (x64) Macs get no build at all. The `dmg:` config block and the `publish: github` provider are inert.
recommendation: Set the mac target to `dmg`/`zip` and add an x64 (or universal) arch entry, or delete the dmg block and document that macOS is arm64-unpacked-only.

title: The npm `original-fs` shim defeats the ASAR-bypass fallback in build attestation
summary: attestation.ts requires 'original-fs' inside a try/catch that falls back to node:fs, expecting the require to fail outside Electron. Declaring the userland original-fs package — which is literally `module.exports=require('fs')` — makes that require always succeed and silently return plain fs.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:127 `"original-fs": "^1.2.0",`. node_modules/original-fs/index.js is one line: `'use strict';module.exports=require('fs');` and its own description reads 'Ensure that the correct module is loaded in a non-Electron environment.' apps/core-app/src/main/modules/build-verification/attestation.ts:109 `physicalFs = requireFromCurrentModule('original-fs') as typeof nodeFs` inside `try { ... } catch { physicalFs = nodeFs }`, feeding :117 `createReadStream` for :121 `hashFileSha256`.
failure_scenario: Electron's built-in original-fs wins inside the main process, so the intended ASAR bypass works there. But in any non-Electron Node context — the utility-process workers declared in apps/core-app/electron.vite.config.ts:209-221, or a plain `node out/main/...` run — the resolver now finds the npm shim instead of throwing, so the catch never fires and the attestation hashes bytes read *through* the ASAR layer rather than the raw archive. The integrity check then compares the wrong bytes without any error.
recommendation: Remove the original-fs dependency so the require genuinely fails outside Electron, or replace the try/catch with an explicit `process.versions.electron` check.

title: extension-loader uses session.loadExtension(), deprecated in Electron 41 in favour of ses.extensions
summary: The Chrome-extension loader calls a session API that Electron 41's own type definitions mark deprecated with a named replacement.
evidence: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/extension-loader.ts:74 `const loaded = await session.defaultSession.loadExtension(fullPath)`. node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:12907-12911 documents it as `**Deprecated:** Use the new ses.extensions.loadExtension API.` followed by `@deprecated` on `loadExtension(path: string, options?: LoadExtensionOptions)`. Electron 41.10.2 exposes the replacement namespace at electron.d.ts:13158 `readonly extensions: Extensions;`. The sibling calls session.removeExtension / getAllExtensions are deprecated in the same release (electron.d.ts:12932, :12791).
failure_scenario: Electron removes deprecated APIs on a two-major cadence, so this call is scheduled to disappear. When it does, ExtensionLoaderModule (module 4 in the documented boot order) throws `session.defaultSession.loadExtension is not a function` during startup and the whole module chain after it fails to initialise.
recommendation: Switch to `session.defaultSession.extensions.loadExtension(...)` (and the matching extensions.remove/getAllExtensions).

title: nuxt.config.ts hardcodes deep node_modules file paths into @panva/hkdf and next-auth internals
summary: Two build aliases point at specific files inside dependency packages, bypassing their exports maps and depending on both the internal dist layout and on hoisting placing them at those exact locations.
evidence: apps/nexus/nuxt.config.ts:47 `const hkdfCompatEntry = resolve(workspaceRoot, 'node_modules/@panva/hkdf/dist/node/cjs/index.js')` and :48 `const nextAuthCoreEntry = resolve(currentDir, 'node_modules/next-auth/core/index.js')`.
failure_scenario: The first path assumes @panva/hkdf keeps its dist/node/cjs layout (the root override pins it to 1.2.1 precisely because of this) AND that .npmrc:1 `shamefully-hoist=true` places it at the workspace root — under a strict pnpm layout the file is inside a .pnpm store path and the alias resolves to a non-existent file, so the Nuxt build fails with an unresolved alias. The second path is a next-auth v4-only internal; next-auth v5 removed the `core/` directory entirely, so any upgrade past 4.24.x breaks the build rather than producing a deprecation error.
recommendation: Resolve both via `import.meta.resolve` / `createRequire(...).resolve(<package specifier>)` instead of literal file paths, and stop reaching past the packages' exports maps.

title: apps/nexus package.json `imports` map points #auth into @sidebase/nuxt-auth's dist internals
summary: The subpath-imports map hard-codes a relative node_modules path into a dependency's compiled runtime, which is neither part of that package's public exports nor stable across its versions.
evidence: apps/nexus/package.json:9-10 `"#auth": "./node_modules/@sidebase/nuxt-auth/dist/runtime/server/services/index.js"` and `"#auth/*": "./node_modules/@sidebase/nuxt-auth/dist/runtime/server/services/*.js"`, against a dependency declared at :51 as `"@sidebase/nuxt-auth": "^0.9.4"` — a caret range on a pre-1.0 package.
failure_scenario: Node's `imports` field resolves relative to the package directory, so this only works when @sidebase/nuxt-auth is physically materialised at apps/nexus/node_modules (a consequence of .npmrc:1 shamefully-hoist=true). Under pnpm's default layout, or after any 0.9.x → 0.10 release that reorganises dist/runtime, every `#auth` import in the Nitro server routes fails to resolve and the API layer will not build.
recommendation: Use the alias the @sidebase/nuxt-auth Nuxt module itself registers, or map #auth through a local re-export file that imports the package by its public specifier.

title: Half the pnpm catalog is dead: 17 of 30 root catalog entries have zero `catalog:` references
summary: The catalog is meant to be the single source of version truth, but most entries are never referenced, and several of those unreferenced entries disagree with the literal versions the packages actually install.
evidence: Scanning every workspace package.json for `"<name>": "catalog:"`, these 17 root-catalog entries have 0 references: @auth/core (pnpm-workspace.yaml:35), @iconify-json/logos (:38), @langchain/anthropic (:39), @langchain/core (:40), @langchain/langgraph (:41), @langchain/openai (:42), @sidebase/nuxt-auth (:44), ai-elements-vue (:45), better-sqlite3 (:46), jsqr (:50), markdown-it (:52), next-auth (:54), nodemailer (:55), openapi-typescript (:57), qrcode (:58), theme-colors (:61), vue-sonner (:64). Three further pseudo-catalogs at :102-107 (`conflicts_next-auth_t4_24_14`, `conflicts_@langchain/langgraph_h0_4_9`, `conflicts_@langchain/openai_h0_4_9`) are likewise referenced by nothing.
failure_scenario: Contributors reading pnpm-workspace.yaml to answer 'what version of X does this repo use?' get wrong answers for langgraph (catalog ^0.2.74 vs installed ^0.4.9), openai (^0.3.17 vs ^0.4.9), next-auth (~4.21.1 vs ~4.24.14) and nodemailer (^9.0.3 vs not installed). Adopting `catalog:` for any of them — the documented convention — silently downgrades the dependency. The conflicts_ catalogs record known version conflicts that were never actually resolved.
recommendation: Delete the unreferenced entries and the conflicts_ catalogs, or convert the real consumers to `catalog:` and correct the versions.

title: tuffex build runs gulp-sass 5.1.0, which uses the Sass legacy JS API removed in Dart Sass 2.0
summary: The component library's style pipeline goes through gulp-sass, which still calls sass.render/renderSync — the legacy API Dart Sass deprecated and will delete in 2.0.
evidence: packages/tuffex/packages/script/build/index.ts:30 and :38 `.pipe(sass())`, driven by packages/tuffex/package.json:45 `"build": "node --loader ts-node/esm ./node_modules/gulp/bin/gulp.js -f packages/script/build/index.ts"`. node_modules/gulp-sass/index.js:145 `gulpSass.compiler.render(opts, ...)` and :158 `gulpSass.compiler.renderSync(opts)`. Verified with the installed sass@1.101.0: calling renderSync prints `DEPRECATION WARNING [legacy-js-api]: The legacy JS API is deprecated and will be removed in Dart Sass 2.0.0.`
failure_scenario: gulp-sass 5.1.0 has no modern-API path. When sass 2.0 ships, bumping the `sass: ^1.101.0` catalog entry (pnpm-workspace.yaml:59) breaks the tuffex build outright with 'sass.renderSync is not a function', taking down the component CSS that apps/core-app, apps/nexus and apps/tuff-analyse all consume from dist/es.
recommendation: Replace gulp-sass with a direct `sass.compile()` step (or a Vite/Rollup style pipeline) before sass 2.0 lands.

title: tuffex build uses `node --loader ts-node/esm`, an experimental flag Node warns may be removed
summary: The component library build depends on the deprecated ESM loader hook flag instead of the supported module.register() entry point.
evidence: packages/tuffex/package.json:45 `"build": "node --loader ts-node/esm ./node_modules/gulp/bin/gulp.js -f packages/script/build/index.ts"`. Running the same flag on the repo's pinned Node (24.18.0, .node-version) prints: `ExperimentalWarning: '--experimental-loader' may be removed in the future; instead use register(): --import 'data:text/javascript,import { register } from "node:module"; ...'` plus `[DEP0180] DeprecationWarning: fs.Stats constructor is deprecated.` from ts-node itself.
failure_scenario: Once Node drops the loader-hook flag, `pnpm tuffex:build` fails with an unknown-option error. Every downstream build depends on it: apps/core-app's `typecheck:web` script (apps/core-app/package.json:17) and apps/nexus's `build` script both invoke `pnpm -F @talex-touch/tuffex run build` first, so the whole repo's typecheck and site build go down together.
recommendation: Switch to `node --import ./register-ts-node.mjs` using module.register(), or run the gulpfile through tsx/esno (esno is already a devDependency).

title: extract-file-icon@0.3.2 ships no prebuilds and pins node-addon-api to an exact 1.7.1
summary: A non-optional native dependency of the shipped app must compile C++ from source on every install, using a six-year-old exact node-addon-api pin that no override can lift.
evidence: apps/core-app/package.json:118 `"extract-file-icon": "^0.3.2",` (in `dependencies`, not `optionalDependencies`). The installed package contains only `binding.gyp build dist lib LICENSE package.json README.md` — no `prebuilds/` directory and no `binary` field — and declares `dependencies: {"node-addon-api":"1.7.1"}` (exact). It is listed in package.json:92 `onlyBuiltDependencies`, so pnpm runs node-gyp against the host toolchain; the sibling native package tuff-native uses node-addon-api ^7.1.1.
failure_scenario: Because it sits in `dependencies` rather than `optionalDependencies` (unlike uiohook-napi and @crosscopy/clipboard, which ship prebuilds), a missing C++ toolchain makes `pnpm install` fail outright for the whole workspace — on any dev machine without Xcode Command Line Tools / MSVC / build-essential, and on any CI image that trims build tools. The exact node-addon-api 1.7.1 pin also means the addon cannot pick up N-API header fixes; it is compiled against Node 24 headers here while the app runs Electron 41 (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 145 vs 137), which only survives because node-addon-api targets the ABI-stable N-API surface.
recommendation: Move it to optionalDependencies with a runtime guard (icon-worker.ts:68 already uses a dynamic import), or replace it with the in-house @talex-touch/tuff-native app-icon binding it already duplicates.

title: onlyBuiltDependencies is stale: 13 of 29 entries absent from the lockfile, fsevents missing
summary: The pnpm build-script allowlist still names packages that were removed from the repo long ago, while a native module that is actually installed is absent from it.
evidence: package.json:92 `"onlyBuiltDependencies": [ ... ]`. Checking each entry against pnpm-lock.yaml snapshots, these 13 have zero entries: @compodoc/compodoc, @google/genai, @nestjs/core, @parcel/watcher, @sentry/cli, @swc/core, browser-tabs-lock, core-js, get-windows, msgpackr-extract, puppeteer, simple-git-hooks, tesseract.js. Meanwhile fsevents@2.3.3 is installed (required by the chokidar 3.6.0 FSEvents backend aliased at apps/core-app/package.json:111 `"chokidar-fsevents": "npm:chokidar@3.6.0"`) but is not listed.
failure_scenario: The stale entries document a dependency set that no longer exists — notably `tesseract.js` and `get-windows`, whose jobs are now done by @talex-touch/tuff-native — so the file misleads anyone auditing which native builds the workspace permits. More concretely, any future native package that needs a build script but is not on the list is silently skipped by pnpm and fails at runtime rather than at install time.
recommendation: Prune the 13 dead entries and add fsevents so the allowlist reflects the packages actually built.
